title: The point of origin of a point-placed area spell (Sleep, Web, ...) isn't checked against the spell's range: _range_check only looks at the targets. Sleep also falls back to 'every listed creature is inside' when no point is given. Require a point for spells whose area sits at a point, and refuse one beyond the spell's range under SPELL.casting-spells.range.

history.reason: The ticket asks to require a point for point-placed area spells, but these acceptance scenarios cast Sleep or Web without one: `tests/scenarios/test_spells.py:158`, `:256` and `:401`, `tests/scenarios/test_magic_items.py:127` and `:133`, and the natural-language Web cast in `tests/scenarios/test_journeys.py:340`. A strict requirement would break them. I implemented a default instead: with no point, the area is centred on the first named creature, and it's refused only when there's no creature either. If a person wants an explicit point required, those scenarios would first need a `point=` (and the natural-language parser a way to name one).
Range-check point= when given; with no point, centre on the first named creature. Don't require a point; don't change the tests.
